Transcript body:
[00:00] Grace: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call, we have Marcus from SE, myself, and from Lyra Samira, Ethan, Maya. How's everyone doing?
[00:12] Samira: Good, thanks. Sorry running a bit late, had an internal standup overrun.
[00:16] Ethan: All good, sounds like we have a packed agenda.
[00:20] Grace: Yeah, main goals — convert pilot into a committed uplift, nail down APAC and EU region plans, and align procurement windows. Marcus, want to kick off on the numbers?
[00:28] Marcus: Sure, yeah. So we've been looking at the pilot telemetry you shared last week — thanks for that, Ethan — and we're proposing two uplift tiers. One is a moderate 2x reserved capacity for production traffic, and the other is a 4x committed for seasonal peaks. The baseline assumption is token distribution avg 35 tokens per request, with a p95 of 220ms in Hosted right now and p99 around 680ms during peak.
[01:05] Ethan: Wait, p99 at 680ms seems ... is that on our test harness or actual traffic? I thought our prod p99 was closer to 400-450.
[01:12] Marcus: That number was from the pilot instances where we didn't have KV prefix caching enabled for the model variants. With KV cache warmed and selective batching we expect p99 to drop to ~420-480ms. The 680ms was a cold path without cache.
[01:30] Samira: Can you explain the caching part again — the K V cache? Sometimes the transcription or our notes call it K V cash which is confusing — ha.
[01:38] Marcus: Yeah sorry, KV cache — key-value cache. It's basically the transformer KV state saved per session so repeated context doesn't recompute. In Redwood we support prefix caching and also per-model cache lifetimes. That helps a lot for our assistant flows where there's a lot of repetition.
[01:56] Ethan: Okay so with caching we should be in line with our SLO. For Lyra we target p95 < 250ms and p99 < 500ms for core assistant queries.
[02:08] Marcus: Correct. With Dedicated capacity and the optimized kernels we can hit those numbers given the token distribution you provided. The tradeoff is cost — Dedicated gives predictable throughput and lower p99s, Hosted is cheaper for variable load but p99 is less consistent.
[02:24] Maya: From procurement perspective, predictability is key. Our CFO wants committed spend but also the ability to scale down after seasonal peaks. How flexible are the contract windows?
[02:33] Grace: We offer quarterly ramp options on Dedicated and burst credit for unexpected spikes. Typically we do a 12‑month reserved commit for the biggest discount, with mid-term scaling add-ons. We can show a few commitment tiers in a spreadsheet — I'll send updated SKUs after this call.
[02:50] Samira: On regions — APAC and EU — what's the lead time to enable those? We have a roadmap to launch APAC in late Q1.
[02:59] Marcus: For Hosted it's near instant once you flip the region flag, but for Dedicated we need a provisioning lead of about 2–4 weeks depending on capacity availability in the site. If you need EU + APAC Dedicated pools, I'd budget 4 weeks to be safe — and if you'd like private VPC peering for EU we'll add on another week for networking and certs.
[03:22] Ethan: Are there any known limits for on-prem or private deployments with Redwood? We're considering a private node for regulated data in EU.
[03:30] Marcus: We support Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem). The on-prem package is more involved: image install, HSM/KMS integration, and customer-managed network. Typical timeline is 6–10 weeks end-to-end for on-prem pilot. Most customers choose Dedicated in-region to start and then evaluate on-prem for later compliance needs.
[03:48] Samira: That matches what we were thinking. For now, we want Dedicated in EU and Hosted in APAC until we validate latency.
[03:56] Grace: Fine compromise. Marcus, can you propose a pilot configuration?
[03:59] Marcus: Suggested pilot: two Dedicated racks in EU-west and one burstable pool in APAC (Hosted fallback). Run 7-day ramp tests at 70%, 90%, 120% traffic to validate autoscale and failover. We'll also run model-quantization experiments — 8-bit quant on the candidate models — to measure quality vs cost.
[04:23] Ethan: On quantization — we need a quality gate. We cannot accept any regression above 2% on our eval set.
[04:30] Marcus: Understood. We'll run A/B evals with your test harness and report delta. We can also pin model versions for rollouts and have automatic fallback to full-precision if quality dips.
[04:42] Maya: For procurement, we need a formal quote and the exact contract start date; our fiscal quarter closes end of December so the PO needs to be in prior. Could we get final numbers by Nov 24?
[04:53] Grace: Yes, we'll aim to deliver pricing and three commitment tiers by Nov 24.
[04:58] Samira: One more thing — security. SOC 2 is required, and we have to do a short audit of KMS/HSM integration and audit logs. Are those in the security packet?
[05:10] Grace: Yes, the SOC2 report and KMS integration notes are in the packet I linked. We also have audit logs and per-request tracing. If you want, we can schedule a security review call with our security engineer.
[05:21] Samira: That would help. Possibly next Tuesday?
[05:24] Grace: We'll follow up with availability.
[05:27] Ethan: On benchmarking access — what's required to run the SE test? We need service account creds or a temporary API key?
[05:33] Marcus: We'll provide a dedicated benchmark key with scoped permissions and limits. I'll also provide the runbook with scripts. Ideally you give us a small subset of production tokens and traffic shapes — obfuscated for PII — so the tests mimic real patterns.
[05:49] Ethan: We'll prepare that and share by Nov 25.
[05:54] Marcus: Perfect. Also note there is an internal fallback routing policy we can enable — route primary requests to Dedicated and overflow to Hosted if Dedicated is saturated; that keeps tail latency bounded while keeping costs manageable.
[06:07] Samira: How does billing look in that overflow scenario? Do we get charged for both?
[06:12] Grace: You'll be billed for the Dedicated reserved capacity monthly, plus any Hosted overflow usage at the Hosted per-token rate. We can model that in the pricing deck so you can see break-even points.
[06:23] Maya: For the PO we need a line itemization — reserved GPU hours, burst credits, support tier — can you break that down?
[06:31] Grace: Absolutely — the SKU sheet will have those broken out. We'll include support levels (standard vs enterprise) and extended SLA options.
[06:40] Samira: Any competitors we should be aware of in terms of feature parity? We're evaluating Anthropic and Vertex for some calls.
[06:47] Marcus: Anthropic has strong models and Vertex is convenient if you already live in GCP. Inferex is another infra vendor that pitches on open-source. Our differentiator here is the production runtime — cache, autoscale, and tooling to keep unit economics predictable.
[07:00] Ethan: Quick question about model variants and rollouts — if we push a model change and see a regression, how fast can we rollback?
[07:07] Marcus: Rollbacks are near-instant with pinned versions. We support canary rollouts and automatic fallback to the previously pinned model if quality drops beyond thresholds you set.
[07:16] Samira: Great. OK logistics — Marcus, you'll own the SE benchmark, Grace the pricing, Ethan will share traffic, and Maya will handle PO timeline. Anything else?
[07:27] Maya: Procurement also needs contract language about data retention and deletion — we require deletion certificates for test data within 30 days after pilot.
[07:35] Grace: Noted — we'll include certification language in the contract addendum.
[07:38] Samira: One last operational item — SSO. We use SAML SSO with SCIM provisioning. Is that supported?
[07:45] Grace: Yes, we support SAML/SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. We'll include SSO configuration docs and Marcus can walk through the SAML metadata in the security call.
[07:56] Ethan: Sounds good. Timeline recap?
[08:00] Grace: Deliver pricing by Nov 24; Lyra to provide traffic profiles by Nov 25; Marcus to run benchmarks and deliver results by Nov 29; procurement PO decisions by Nov 30. Security deep-dive to be scheduled in the next week.
[08:14] Samira: That works.
[08:17] Marcus: Quick note — for the APAC pool, there's a potential hardware constraint in a couple regions. If you need very low p99 in APAC we may need a slightly different instance type; I'll flag that in the benchmark report.
[08:30] Ethan: Ack. We'll watch for that.
[08:33] Grace: Anything else from Lyra?
[08:36] Maya: Not from procurement — just need the asset list for the PO.
[08:39] Samira: No more questions. Thanks everyone.
[08:42] Grace: Great, thanks all. I'll follow up with the pricing sheet and deck. Marcus will follow up on the runbook. Meeting adjourned.

Notes on transcription quality: occasional speaker misattribution and shorthand replaced (e.g., K V cash -> KV cache; some model names truncated). Transcript captures fillers and short crosstalk.
